about: This wine comes from Grace Tyler Estate Winery in Constantia, on the north shore of Oneida Lake. Richard and Elizabeth Hamilton founded it after buying the land in 2012. They planted cold-hardy vines, picked their first harvest in 2017 and opened the doors in 2018. The winery has since collected regional medals, and its skin-fermented La Crescent is one of the more adventurous bottles in the lineup.

La Crescent is a Muscat-descended hybrid bred at the University of Minnesota to survive deep cold. It is usually made as a fresh, aromatic white. Here the juice is fermented on its skins, the way red wine is made, so the wine draws color, texture and gentle tannin from the skins. The result is an amber or “orange” style. Skin contact turns the grape’s apricot perfume deeper and more savory.

Expect apricot, orange peel and tropical fruit, with notes of tea, dried flowers and citrus zest: it reads like a classic orange wine. A firmer grip makes it a good match for roasted vegetables, cured meats and dishes from the hearth. Compare it with the winery’s fresh, semi-dry La Crescent, also on this list, to see how much skin contact changes the same grape.
